p: I saw also the Lord sitting: God does not show himself to man in his majesty but according as man's capacity to comprehend him, that is, by visible signs as John the Baptist saw the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove.
throne: As a judge ready to give sentence.
train filled the temple: Of his garment, or of his throne.
seraphims: They were angels so called because they were of a fiery colour, to signify that they burnt in the love of God, or were light as fire to execute his will.
face: Signifying that they were not able to endure the brightness of God's glory.
feet: By which it was declared that man was not able to see the brightness of God in them.
flew: Which declares the prompt obedience of the angels to execute God's commandment.
Holy: This often repetition signifies that the angels cannot satisfy themselves in praising God, to teach us that in all our lives we should give ourselves to the continual praise of God.
earth is full of his glory: His glory not only appears in the heavens but through all the world, and therefore all creatures are bound to praise him.
moved at the voice of him: Which was to confirm the prophet, that it was not the voice of man: and by the smoke was signified the blindness that would come on the Jews.

Woe is me: He speaks this for two reasons, the one because he who was a mortal creature and therefore had more need to glorify God than the angels, did not do it, and the other because the nearer that man approaches to God, the more he knows his own sin and corruption.
altar: Of the burnt offerings where the fire never went out.
sin purged: This declares that man cannot render due obedience to God, till he has purged us.

Hear ye indeed: By which is declared that for the malice of man God will not immediately take away his word, but he will cause it to be preached to their condemnation, when as they will not learn by it to obey his will, and be saved: by this he exhorts the ministers to do their duty, and answers to the wicked murmurers, that through their own malice their heart is hardened, Mt 13:14, Ac 28:26, Ro 11:8.
how long: As he was moved with the zeal of God's glory, so was he touched with a charitable affection toward the people.
a tenth: Meaning, the tenth part: or as some write, it was revealed to Isaiah for the confirmation of his prophecy that ten kings would come before their captivity, as were from Uzziah to Zedekiah.
and as an oak: For the fewness of them they will seem to be eaten up: yet they will later flourish as a tree, which in winter loses leaves, and seems to be dead, yet in summer is fresh and green.
